items.title: The naive cotangent complex of a colimit of ring maps is the colimit of the naive cotangent complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a directed system of ring maps the lemma states that the naive cotangent complex of the colimit is the colimit of the naive cotangent complexes (statement lines 35773-35779). The proof does not verify the universal property of the complex or construct comparison maps by hand: it recalls that the complex is built from the kernel I of the canonical presentation, notes that the polynomial algebra and that kernel both commute with the directed colimit, and reads the conclusion off termwise (proof lines 35781-35789). Recognising that the definition reduces the question to two colimit commutations is the content of the argument. H2.
